question: At what approximate date is the earth furthest from the sun (aphelion)?

options.text: Beginning of July.
End of December.
Beginning of January.
End of September.

explanation: Aphelion (furthest from the Sun) is around 4 July; perihelion around 3 January.

question: Observed from a position on the surface of the Earth the heavenly bodies seems to:

options.text: not change their relative positions on the sky.
move from West to East on the southern hemisphere.
move from East to West on the northern hemisphere.
move from East to West.

explanation: Because the Earth rotates west to east, all heavenly bodies appear to move from east to west in both hemispheres.

question: The direction of the Earth’s rotation on its axis is such that:

options.text: Observed from the point above the North Pole, the rotation is counter-clockwise.
An observer on the surface of the earth always will face West when observing sunrise.
Any point on the surface of the Earth will move eastward.
Any point on the surface of the Earth will move westward.

explanation: Seen from above the North Pole the Earth rotates counter-clockwise (west to east).

question: What is the angle between the plane of the Ecliptic and the plane of the Equator?
explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted 23½° to the perpendicular of its orbit, so the ecliptic is inclined 23½° to the equator.

question: What is the approximate latitude of the Antarctic Circle?
explanation: Antarctic Circle ≈ 66½°S (90° − 23½°).

question: Seasons are due to the:

options.text: Earths elliptical orbit around the Sun.
inclination of the polar axis with the ecliptic plane.
Earths rotation on its polar axis.
variable distance between Earth and Sun.

explanation: Seasons result from the 23½° inclination of the Earth's axis to the plane of its orbit (ecliptic).

question: The suns declination is on a particular day 12.00 S. Midnight sun may this day be observed:

options.text: North of 7800S.
South of 7800S.
At 7800S only.
North of 7800N.

explanation: Midnight sun occurs within (90° − declination) of the pole on the same side: south of 78°S.

question: What is the approximate date of perihelion, when the Earth is nearest to the Sun?

options.text: Beginning of January.
End of December.
Beginning of July.
End of March.

explanation: Perihelion ≈ 3 January.

question: The planets move around the Sun:

options.text: In circular orbits.
In elliptical orbits.
At constant angular speed.
At constant velocity.

explanation: Kepler's first law: planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus.

question: The term sidereal is used:

options.text: to describe how two positions of heavenly bodies are located sideways on the sky.
to describe conditions with reference to the moon.
to describe a situation or relationship concerning the stars.
to describe the time interval between two successive transits of the real apparent sun at the same meridian.

explanation: Sidereal refers to the stars (e.g. sidereal day/year measured against the fixed stars).

question: Atmospheric refraction:

options.text: Causes the Sunrise and the Sunset to occur earlier.
Causes the Sunrise and the Sunset to occur later.
Causes the Sunrise to occur later and the Sunset to occur earlier.
Cause the Sunrise to occur earlier and the Sunset to occur later.

explanation: Refraction lifts the Sun's image, so it is seen before it actually rises and after it actually sets: earlier sunrise, later sunset.

question: Assuming mid-latitudes (40° to 50° N/S). At which time of year is the relationship between the length of day and night, as well as the rate of change of declination of the sun, changing at the greatest rate?

options.text: Summer solstice and spring equinox.
Spring equinox and autumn equinox.
Summer solstice and winter solstice.
Winter solstice and autumn equinox.

explanation: At the equinoxes the Sun's declination changes fastest, so day/night length changes most rapidly.

question: As seen from an observer on the surface of the earth:

options.text: the sun is in a fixed position relative to the stars.
the stars will seem to move from west to east during a year.
the suns position relative to the stars is fixed throughout the year.
the apparent sun is always in the plane of the ecliptic.

explanation: The ecliptic is by definition the Sun's apparent path, so the apparent Sun is always on it.

question: What is the highest latitude listed below at which the sun will reach an altitude of 90° above the horizon at some time during the year?
explanation: The Sun can be overhead only between the tropics: max latitude ≈ 23½°.

question: Which is the highest latitude listed below at which the sun will rise above the horizon and set every day?
explanation: The Sun rises and sets every day only below the polar circles (66½°): 66°.

question: When the suns declination is northerly:

options.text: it is winter on the northern hemisphere.
the sunrise occurs earlier at southern latitudes than the northern latitudes.
the daylight period is shorter in the southern hemisphere than the northern.
midnight sun may be observed at the south pole.

explanation: With northerly declination it is summer in the northern hemisphere; daylight is shorter in the southern hemisphere.

question: The main reason that day and night, throughout the year, have different durations is due to the:

options.text: earths rotation.
relative speed of the sun along the ecliptic.
inclination of the ecliptic to the equator.
gravitational effect of the Sun and the Moon on the speed of rotation of the Earth.

explanation: Unequal day and night are caused by the inclination of the ecliptic to the equator (axial tilt).

question: The time it takes for the Earth to complete one orbit around the Sun is:

options.text: 360 days 45 hours, 5 minutes 48 seconds.
360 days 5 hours 45 minutes 48 seconds.
365 days 45 hours 48 minutes 5 seconds.
365 days 5 hours 48 minutes 45 seconds.

explanation: The tropical year ≈ 365 d 5 h 48 min 45 s.

question: In its path around the Sun, the axis of the Earth has an inclination:

options.text: varying between zero and 23° 27 with the plane of the pat.
of 66º 33 with the plane of the path.
varying with the season of the year.
of 23º 27 with the plane of Equator.

explanation: The axis is inclined 66°33′ to the orbital plane (i.e. 23°27′ from the perpendicular).

question: The suns declination is:

options.text: The suns position relative to the plane of the Equator.
The distance between the sun and the horizon.
The angular distance between the sun and the celestial North Pole.
The suns position relative to the ecliptic.

explanation: Declination is the Sun's angular position north or south of the plane of the celestial equator.

question: The inclination of the earth’s axis of rotation with the plane of the ecliptic:

options.text: is causing the variation of length of the daylight during a year.
is stable throughout the year.
is causing the seasons, summer and winter.
All 3 answers are correct.

explanation: The constant 23½° tilt causes the seasons and the variation in daylight length — all correct.

question: What is the length of a sidereal year?

options.text: 365 days
365 days 6 hours
365 days 5 hours 48.75 minutes

explanation: The sidereal year (one orbit measured against the stars) is ≈ 365 d 6 h 9 min. 365 d 5 h 48¾ min is the tropical (seasons) year, on which the calendar is based.

question: Which statement about the duration of daylight is true?

options.text: Close to the equinoxes the influence of latitude on the duration of daylight is at its smallest
Close to the solstices the influence of latitude on the duration of daylight is at its smallest
At the Equator daylight varies by about two hours through the year
Daylight duration depends on longitude as well as latitude

explanation: At the equinoxes the Sun is over the Equator and day ≈ night ≈ 12 h almost everywhere, so latitude makes the least difference.
